doc.title: Claude Williams interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995

title: T. Holder's band and the jitney dance at Le Louvre
summary: He recalls the T. Holder band that became Andy Kirk's and the ticket dances at Le Louvre in Tulsa, with a Ford given away weekly.

bands.name: Andy Kirk's Twelve Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Tell us some of the other musicians that you’ve played with.

Oh, I really can’t think of all the names. But I’ve been with so many different, uh, I was originally was with it turned out to be Andy Kirk’s Twelve Clouds of Joy. It was first a fellow by the name of T. Holder. And T. Holder was from Muskogee also, that was my home. And he came in, and first he had a band in Tulsa by the name of Le Louvre. You ever know anything about a jitney dance? You ever heard of a jitney dance?
Uh, no, tell me, tell me. I think this is something new for me.

Well this was at Le Louvre, in Tulsa. And a jitney dance is a ten cents dance thing like a man would go and buy a roll of tickets and then go back and ask a lady to dance and if you want to dance. And there was a few fellows standing at the gate there and you’d go by and hand him these tickets. And when you get enough in this ring, he’d call out, “And now we’ll have a foxtrot.” So we had to be ready to play that foxtrot right then. And we’d play about maybe two choruses and he’d blow the whistle and that’s the end of that. And he’d go by and ring you off and by the time you’d get them all off there’d be another

bunch going in. And every time you’d go into the ring you’d ask some lady to give a ticket. And why they were making so much money then, they gave away a brand new Ford every Friday night, if you held the right ticket, you know. You’d tear your ticket off and you’d keep the stub you know. And you’d put your stub, part of the stub tickets in the thing where they’d drop it. And they’d go in there and at the end of the week and feel around and 892 or something like that, that’s you. You got a brand new Ford.
